title: I built a ML model recently ...
author: Civil_Bear_4448
selftext:
Follow-up to my last post. A lot of you asked how it actually performs, so I tested it the right way this time: held out the most recent data, compared against just guessing the majority class, and looked at false alarms instead of only accuracy.

It's basically a coin flip. The accuracy looked fine until I put the baseline next to it, then the gap mostly vanished. The drawdown warning does catch more events if you lower the cutoff, but it cries wolf constantly.Kind of a letdown, but I'd rather know. I've since turned it into a small research tool where you can upload your own price CSV and see how a model really does against a baseline. And i need help , if there is anyone having knowledge and experience in Fintech or ML

it would be great if you poke around a Lil bit .

comments.author: FailedMouse
comments.body: Well, machine learning is not simple. ML confidence varies and depends on many factors, signal quality, count, retrain cadence, features themselves, if they used and trained in right manner. You didn't give much context there. Blaming ML is naive without telling what did you ask ML to learn? Did you use set tp/sl? Learned from timeout events or only on tp's reached in their window? Did you select few features or showed too many in there? How much data did you actually let it train on? Maybe model starved or maybe it was fed noise? Getting ML confidence over 0.5 is very hard. Personally I never saw higher than 0.55 on direction model

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: The baseline killing the gap is honestly the most useful result here, most people never add one. For the drawdown alert I'd look at what a false alarm actually costs you. If it just means cutting size for a few days, crying wolf might be fine.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
coin flip once the baseline sits next to it is a result most people never get to, so that's progress. accuracy and money also come apart: a model that's right on the few big days beats one that's right often on quiet ones, so score it on what the trades would have made after fills. I built Quantradin after hitting that gap, you write the rule and it replays it on real past prices, paper only. quantradin.com

what horizon is it predicting, next bar or next day?
